blocks.title: Core Concepts: Respiratory Organs
blocks.text:
Introduction :-

  • Respiration : a metabolic process where an organism obtains energy (in the form of ATP) by taking in ${O_2}$ and liberating ${CO_2}$  from the oxidation of complex organic substances.
  • Breathing : a physical process by which oxygen is taken in and carbon dioxide is given out.
Respiratory organs in different organisms :-

  • Entire body surface → Sponges, coelenterates, flatworms
  • Moist cuticle → Earthworms
  • Tracheal tubes (Network of tubes) → Insects
  • Gills → Aquatic arthropods, molluscs, fishes
  • Lungs → Amphibians, Reptiles, birds, mammals
Amphibian (frog) :-

Larva (Tadpole):

  • by gills
Adult :

• by moist skin, buccal cavity and lungs

blocks.title: Respiratory Organs
blocks.text:
→ Nose and Nasal Chamber

  • External nostrils: 1 pair.
  • Nasal passage opens into nasal chamber.
  • Nasal chamber opens into pharynx (Common passage for food and air).
→ Larynx

  • Responsible for sound production (Sound box).
  • Vocal cords are present on larynx (true and false vocal cords).
  • Epiglottis (elastic cartilaginous flap) covers glottis during swallowing.
→ Trachea

  • Straight tube.
  • Extending up to the mid-thoracic cavity.
  • Divides at the level of ${5^{th}}$ thoracic vertebra into a right and left primary bronchi.
  • Trachea, 1°, 2° and 3° bronchi and initial bronchioles → C-shaped Incomplete cartilaginous rings.
→ Diaphragm

  • Principal muscle of breathing and aid in ventilation.
→ Intercostal muscles: two types –

  • (1) External intercostal muscles (EICM): Inspiratory muscles
  • (2) Internal intercostal muscles (IICM): Expiratory muscles
→ Thoracic cavity & Respiratory muscles

Thoracic chamber is formed

  • Dorsally → Vertebral column
  • Ventrally → Sternum
  • Laterally → The ribs
  • Lower side → Diaphragm
→ Alveoli

  • Structural and functional units of lungs.
  • The total number of alveoli present in the lungs of man is 300 million.
→ Lungs

  • 2 lungs covered by a double layered pleura, with pleural fluid between them.
  • Pleural fluid acts as a shock absorber.
  • Situated in thoracic chamber.

blocks.title: Question.1
blocks.question:
Which of the following is not the function of the conducting part of the respiratory system?

(1) Inhaled air is humidified

(2) Temperature of inhaled air is brought to body temperature

(3) Provides surface for diffusion of $O_2$  and $CO_2$

(4) It clears inhaled air from foreign particles
blocks.answer:
Answer:3

Explanation:

  • The conducting part of the respiratory system (nasal cavity, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, and terminal bronchioles) serves to filter, warm, humidify, and clear air of foreign particles.
  • It does not participate in gas exchange, as that function is carried out by the respiratory part (respiratory bronchioles, alveolar ducts, and alveoli).
  • Gas exchange (diffusion of O₂ and CO₂) occurs only in the respiratory part.
options: (2) Temperature of inhaled air is brought to body temperature
(4) It clears inhaled air from foreign particles

blocks.title: Question.2
blocks.question:
Lungs are covered by

(1) Perichondrium

(2) Pleural sac

(3) Pericardium

(4) Peristomium
blocks.answer:
The correct answer is:

(2) Pleural sac

Explanation:

  • The lungs are covered by a double-layered membrane called the pleural sac, which consists of:
  • • Visceral pleura: Directly covers the lungs.
      • Parietal pleura: Lines the thoracic cavity.

blocks.title: Question.3
blocks.question:
Which statement is correct ?

(1) Pulmonary ventilation is equal to alveolar ventilation.

(2) Pulmonary ventilation is less than alveolar ventilation.

(3) Alveolar ventilation is more than Pulmonary ventilation.

(4) Alveolar ventilation is less than Pulmonary ventilation.
blocks.answer:
The correct answer is:

(4) Alveolar ventilation is less than Pulmonary ventilation.

Explanation:

  • Pulmonary ventilation is the total volume of air moved in and out of the lungs per minute, including both the air reaching the alveoli and the air in the anatomical dead space (airways where gas exchange does not occur).
  • Alveolar ventilation refers to the volume of air that actually reaches the alveoli and is available for gas exchange.
  • Due to the presence of dead space, alveolar ventilation is always less than pulmonary ventilation.
options: (1) Pulmonary ventilation is equal to alveolar ventilation.
(2) Pulmonary ventilation is less than alveolar ventilation.
(3) Alveolar ventilation is more than Pulmonary ventilation.
(4) Alveolar ventilation is less than Pulmonary ventilation.

blocks.title: Exchange of gases
blocks.text:
Site of gases exchange :
    • Alveoli- The primary site
    • Between blood and tissues

The exchange of gases occurs through simple diffusion and the rate of diffusion is affected by :
    • Pressure/concentration gradients
    • Solubility of gases
    • Thickness of the membrane
The solubility of CO₂ is 20-25 times higher than that of O₂; therefore, the amount of CO₂ that can diffuse through the diffusion membrane per unit difference in partial pressure is much higher compared to that of O₂. This higher solubility compensates for the lower diffusion gradient of CO₂, ensuring efficient gas exchange in the lungs.

blocks.title: Common Mistake
blocks.text:
• Gas exchange occurs due to differences in partial pressure of gases (O₂ and CO₂) between the alveoli and blood.

  • Forgetting that gases move from areas of high partial pressure to areas of low partial pressure (down a gradient).

blocks.title: Question 1
blocks.question:
The bulk of carbon dioxide (CO₂) released from body tissues into the blood is present as :

(1) Carbamino-haemoglobin in RBCs

(2) Bicarbonate in blood plasma and RBCs

(3) Free CO₂ in blood plasma

(4) 70% carbamino-haemoglobin and 30% as bicarbonate
blocks.answer:
The correct answer is:

(2) Bicarbonate in blood plasma and RBCs

Explanation:

  • The majority (about 70%) of carbon dioxide (CO₂) released from body tissues into the blood is transported as bicarbonate (HCO₃⁻) in the plasma and inside red blood cells (RBCs).
  • Carbaminohemoglobin (CO₂ bound to hemoglobin) accounts for about 20% of CO₂ transport.
  • A small fraction (about 10%) remains dissolved as free CO₂ in the blood plasma.
options: (2) Bicarbonate in blood plasma and RBCs

blocks.title: Question.2
blocks.question:
Assertion: Oxygen dissociation curve is sigmoid.

Reason: The affinity of oxygen for Hb increases with the addition of each molecule of oxygen one after another.

(1) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.

(2) Assertion is true but the reason is false.

(3) Both the assertion and reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion.

(4) Both assertion and reason are false
blocks.answer:
Answer:1

Explanation:

  • The oxygen dissociation curve for hemoglobin (Hb) is sigmoid (S-shaped) due to the cooperative binding of oxygen molecules to hemoglobin. As each molecule of oxygen binds to hemoglobin, it causes a conformational change that increases the affinity for subsequent oxygen molecules.
  • The reason correctly explains the assertion: as each oxygen molecule binds to hemoglobin, it increases the affinity for the next oxygen molecule, which causes the curve to become steeper as more oxygen binds. This is why the curve is sigmoid-shaped.
options: (1) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
(2) Assertion is true but the reason is false.
(3) Both the assertion and reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
(4) Both assertion and reason are false
blocks.prompt:
Assertion: Oxygen dissociation curve is sigmoid.

Reason: The affinity of oxygen for Hb increases with the addition of each molecule of oxygen one after another.

blocks.title: Question.3
blocks.question:
The exchange of bicarbonates and chloride ions between RBC and plasma is called:-

(1) Chloride shift.

(2) Bohr's effect.

(3) Haldane's effect.

(4) Intracellular respiration
blocks.answer:
The correct answer is:

(1) Chloride shift.

Explanation:

  • The chloride shift (also called the Hamburger phenomenon) refers to the exchange of bicarbonate ions (HCO₃⁻) and chloride ions (Cl⁻) between red blood cells (RBCs) and plasma.
  • As CO₂ enters the RBCs, it reacts with water to form carbonic acid, which dissociates into bicarbonate and hydrogen ions. The bicarbonate ions move out of the RBCs into the plasma, and chloride ions move into the RBCs to maintain electrical neutrality.

blocks.title: Question 1
blocks.question:
Q. Assertion: Emphysema is a chronic disorder in which the respiratory surface is decreased.

Reason: One of the major causes of this is cigarette smoking.

(1) Assertion is true but the reason is false.

(2) Assertion is false but Reason is true.

(3) Assertion and Reason both are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.

(4) Assertion and Reason both are true and Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.
blocks.answer:
The correct answer is: 3

Assertion and Reason both are true and Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

Explanation:

  • Assertion: Emphysema is indeed a chronic disorder in which the respiratory surface is decreased, primarily due to the destruction of the alveolar walls, leading to reduced surface area for gas exchange.
  • Reason: One of the major causes of emphysema is cigarette smoking, which contributes to lung damage and the destruction of alveolar tissue. The correct reason is damage to the Alveolar wall. Cigarette smoking does not directly link with Assertion.
options: (1) Assertion is true but the reason is false.
(2) Assertion is false but Reason is true.
(3) Assertion and Reason both are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.
(4) Assertion and Reason both are true and Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.
blocks.prompt:
Q. Assertion: Emphysema is a chronic disorder in which the respiratory surface is decreased.

Reason: One of the major causes of this is cigarette smoking.
